title: Why are they called triangular, square and cube numbers?
description: Dots stack into a triangle, fill a square grid, or build a cube of blocks. The video shows the shape behind each name and checks the fifth number of each kind.
teaching_notes: One idea: each name comes from the shape the dots or blocks make. Watch for students who think the names are only labels.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (Math Talk), p.5
video_script.why: The child sees the shape behind each name: dots in rows make a triangle, n rows of n dots make a square, and n by n by n blocks make a cube.
video_script.substitution: A number takes the name of the shape its dots or blocks make.
video_script.anchor: three groups of pictures: stacked rows of dots, a square grid of dots and a cube of blocks
video_script.payoff_line: Each name is the shape that the dots or blocks make

final_answer.value: Triangular: that many dots can be arranged in a triangle (rows of 1, 2, 3, ...). Square: that many dots form a square grid (n rows of n). Cubes: that many unit blocks form a cube (n by n by n).
final_answer.spoken: each name is the shape that the dots or blocks make

hold_back: Each name is the shape that the dots or blocks make
maths_rules: triangular: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 dots stack in rows of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, which makes a triangle
square: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 dots fill a square grid, 1 by 1, 2 by 2, 3 by 3, 4 by 4, 5 by 5
cubes: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 blocks build a cube, 1 by 1 by 1, 2 by 2 by 2 and so on
video_script.design: One idea: the name comes from the shape. Callback to why ten is called triangular. Wrong idea: none is broken. The three shapes stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about three kinds of numbers.
<bookmark mark='names'/>They are called triangular, square and cube numbers.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Why does each kind get its name?

narration: <bookmark mark='pile'/>A number of dots can be laid out in a shape.
<bookmark mark='shape'/>If the dots fit a shape with none left over, the number can be named after that shape.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, triangular: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 dots stack in rows of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 dots, which makes a triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step one, triangular. The dots of one, three, six, ten and fifteen stack in rows.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>The rows have one, two, three, four and five dots. Each stack is a triangle.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, square: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 dots fill a square grid: 1 by 1, 2 by 2, 3 by 3, 4 by 4, 5 by 5

marks.sq: the dots of each square number fill a square grid

narration: <bookmark mark='sq'/>Step two, square. The dots of one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five fill a square grid.
<bookmark mark='grids'/>The grids are one by one, two by two, and three by three. The last two are four by four and five by five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, cubes: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 blocks build a cube: 1 by 1 by 1, 2 by 2 by 2, and so on

marks.cube: the blocks of each cube number build a cube
marks.sizes: each cube is labelled with its equal length, width and height

narration: <bookmark mark='cube'/>Step three, cubes. The blocks of one, eight, twenty seven, sixty four and one hundred twenty five build a cube.
<bookmark mark='sizes'/>The cubes are one by one by one, two by two by two, and so on.

beats.on_screen: Check, the fifth of each: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15, 5 x 5 = 25, 5 x 5 x 5 = 125

marks.check: a tick appears beside the fifth triangle
marks.more: a tick appears beside the fifth square and the fifth cube

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the fifth number of each kind. Five rows add up to fifteen.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Five times five is twenty five. Five times five times five is one hundred twenty five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Each name is the shape that the dots or blocks make
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each name is the shape that the dots or blocks make.
